A small west entrance porch and stair/lift core sit in the notch below the short wing.
pages.confidence: High for L topology and 1F absence of bridge; secondary external stairs are approximate.

notes: Text explicitly says the bridge at the end of the left corridor connects to the north building.
Bridge enters the western tip of the short wing at corridor level, not the end of the long stem.
The long bridge run, its elbow cross, and the right-facing short run duplicate the north 2F bridge and are suitable registration constraints.
The grid below the west stair/lobby return appears as roof/glazing/projection and must not be assumed to be an additional full enclosed room.
Main leg width nearly matches north long-bar depth in the 2F drawings (138 versus 138 image pixels), supporting a shared plan scale.
pages.confidence: High for bridge registration and occupied L; the grid interpretation is bounded and secondary.

notes: Same principal L and small west stair/lobby return as lower south floors after accounting for the larger drawing scale.
Main stem nominal width is approximately 204 pixels, and short wing 319 pixels; the ratio is 0.64, closely matching the 2F ratio 138/217.
Third floor has no bridge. Do not stack the connection at 3F.
Small corridor-end protrusions are visible at the extreme west/east of the short wing and around the south stair; simplify only with explicit scale/manufacturing disclosure.
pages.confidence: High for three floors and L shape; no independent absolute scale.

registration.reference: north 2F PNG main-bar top-left (265,499); nominal long-bar width 405 px assigned 100 model units.
registration.unit: Model units may be interpreted as mm if author chooses north main bar = 100 mm. No real-world meters are inferred.
registration_evidence: Bridge vertical side lines: north x615/634 versus south x397/416 -> +218 px.
Bridge elbow horizontal rail: north y861/879 versus south y599/618 -> +261 to +262 px.
Bridge north endpoint y692 versus south upper cutoff y433 -> +259 px; drawings do not encode exactly identical cut lines. Use an approximately 2 px tolerance.
North bar depth about 138 px and south long-leg width about 138 px independently support the common scale.
registration.formula: x=(x_northPNG-265)/4.05; y=(y_northPNG-499)/4.05; for south2 use x_northPNG=x_southPNG+218, y_northPNG=y_southPNG+261.

bridge_model.note: Elbow has a short left and south nub in the official plan. Shape is a narrow bridge; preserve open air below instead of extending these rectangles down to grade.

south_model.note: Body length 68.9 includes crosswing plus long leg; 82.0 includes the stair projection. Do not substitute 76 units as an apparently measured length.

hall_model_approx.source: North1 fan shell scaled by north1 495 px long-bar width, checked against north2 roof projection.
hall_model_approx.note: Only shell horizontal plan is constrained. Roof rise, lower hall eaves and vertical joining height must be explicit estimates.

observations: Map locates the northern and southern Marine Science and Technology bodies as a connected group distinct from existing other-campus packages.
A narrow inter-building link and open surrounding ground are visible in the historical campus diagram.
Map is a 2018 accessibility configuration and does not establish 2026 conditions, exact floor heights, or solar-panel count.
The map orientation differs from the plan-page coordinate convention; do not identify image-left/image-right with west/east geographic bearings without a separate rotation.

constraints_and_limits: No dimension chain, survey scale, precise story heights or roof construction drawings were found in these supplied PDFs.
Do not claim measured dimensions or all floors at the same height.
Conference hall is part of north building, a low single-floor occupied body with roof projections in 2F/3F; it is not a separate package or additional 2F/3F room.
North occupied four-floor main body, south occupied three-floor body; the connection occurs only at 2F.
Do not fill the courtyard or bridge undercroft, or the north porch below the 3F/4F west wing.
Interior equipment, chairs, room partitions and source raster artwork are not publication deliverables.
This review is source/geometry evidence only. Mesh, fits, support accessibility and actual slicer checks are separate checks.
